dossier.public_summary: The dips alternate deep and shallow every transit and the depth changes dramatically between instruments and sectors, so they are not a steady planet on the target. The long, grazing shape and two unusually deep dips match a diluted eclipsing binary or blend folded at the wrong period rather than a small planet.

reasons.why: Odd and even dips differ at >4 sigma with a large depth ratio, as expected for an eclipsing binary folded at half its period (true binary period 2 x 9.23 d = 18.5 d). The per-sector odd-even checks also show odd depths much larger than even (sector_oe_max_sigma 3.777, sector_oe_sectors_over_3 1).

Individual transit depths are highly inconsistent and driven by a few deep events (top 3 carry 0.922 of the signal, with two outliers near 1000 ppm vs a mean of 406 ppm). Photometric outliers imply blended or systematic eclipses rather than a steady planet on the target.
reasons.value: p_consistent 1.9500451773854894e-16 chi2 91.86 dof 8 share_of_top_3 0.922 outliers depth_ppm 1011 sigma 4.9 and 1002 sigma 4.7; mean_depth_ppm 406

reasons.why: Depth varies strongly between sectors; sector_depths_by_source gives verdict differs_by_source with QLP 96 ppm err 43 steady (p 0.42) vs SPOC 2-min 625 ppm err 73 (p 0.021). A true on-target planet should not appear with near-zero depth in QLP and deep in SPOC, supporting an extended blend/calibration-dependent false alarm.
